rationale.text: Tile the M-dimension (i) with factor 128. This creates 512/128=4 outer tiles along M. Combined with J tiling this gives thread-blocks of 128×128 output elements — a standard large-GEMM tile that maximises arithmetic intensity and reuse of A rows from shared memory while fitting within the 49 KB SMEM budget on Ampere.

Tile the N-dimension (j) with factor 128. Creates 4 outer tiles along N, giving a 4×4=16 output-block grid across 30 SMs for good occupancy. The 128×128 output tile drives high register reuse for B columns. Together i=128, j=128 provides the canonical GEMM tile that amortises DRAM traffic.

Tile the K reduction axis with factor 32. This sets the shared-memory staging depth: each iteration loads a 128×32 slice of A and a 32×128 slice of B into SMEM (128×32×2 bytes × 2 = 32 KB for FP32 — well within 49 KB), enabling the outer K loop to stream through the full K=512 in 16 steps while keeping data in fast SMEM.

Map the outer i-tile loop (4 tiles of 128) to threadblock.x. This distributes the M-dimension work across SM grid columns, enabling 4 independent thread-blocks along M to run concurrently on separate SMs.

Map the outer j-tile loop (4 tiles of 128) to threadblock.y. Combined with i→threadblock.x, this creates a 4×4=16 thread-block grid which covers all 30 SMs with two waves (first 16 blocks + 14 from a second wave), giving high SM utilization for the 512×512 problem.

Vectorize the inner j loop with width=4. On Ampere this emits 128-bit (float4) memory loads/stores, maximising memory-bus utilization and enabling the hardware's memory coalescing. Width 4 is the sweet-spot that fits register capacity within a 128-wide j tile.

Unroll the inner k loop by factor 4. With k tile=32, this unrolls 4 iterations of the inner-most accumulation loop, reducing loop-control overhead and enabling the instruction scheduler to hide latency through instruction-level parallelism (ILP) across the 4 unrolled FMAs.

Map the inner i-loop (128 elements) to warp-level parallelism. This subdivides the i-tile among warps within each thread-block, exposing 128/32=4 warps along M. Combined with j on threadblock.y, this enables warp-level data partitioning that keeps each warp's register file busy and allows the SM scheduler to hide memory-access latency via warp interleaving.

Unroll the inner i-loop by factor 4 to expose ILP along the M-dimension within each warp's register tile. Each unrolled iteration computes a separate row accumulator, and the compiler/scheduler can overlap independent FMA chains — reducing the effective critical-path latency of the reduction loop.

Unroll the inner j-loop by factor 4 to complement the j-vectorization (width=4 × unroll=4 = 16 j-elements per thread iteration). This exposes 4 independent FMA chains along the N-dimension per warp, saturating the Ampere SM's dual FP32 FMA pipelines and hiding pipeline latency.
